answer: Give each identity a chain of errands revealed one at a time: serve a stranger, collect their receipt, and only then learn the next stop. The chain twists like a vine because every receipt branches to a different counterparty, so assignments wander instead of repeating. A sybil operator cannot batch a thousand puppets through one script; each chain diverges, demands real sequential work at an honest pace, and stalls on the same knoll when one link fails, so extra identities multiply labor rather than influence.
